home.hero_title: Every sound has a shape, and every child has a voice.
home.hero_copy: Shape My Sound turns speech practice into play: a calm, multisensory world where kids build communication confidence through sound, shape, and movement.
home.how_title: A calm path from sound to confidence
home.how_copy: Three gentle steps, built around how children naturally learn: through play, senses, and joy.
home.how_step1_copy: Children meet Bouba and Kiki and explore playful sounds. No pressure, just curiosity.
home.how_step2_copy: Each sound becomes a soft, colorful shape, turning abstract speech into something kids can see and touch.
home.how_step3_copy: Gentle movement and celebration turn practice into confidence that carries into the real world.
home.metrics_copy: Everything a child needs to start practicing, in one calm place.
home.science_title: Built on how the brain connects sound and meaning
home.science_copy: The Bouba/Kiki effect shows that people everywhere link rounded sounds to soft shapes and sharp sounds to spiky ones. Shape My Sound turns that natural cross-sensory wiring into a learning tool.
home.parents_copy: A warm, clear dashboard shows how your child is growing: confidence trends, practice streaks, and gentle next steps.

home.partner_copy: We work with NGOs, schools, and clinics to reach the children who need it most.

practice.title: Practice activities
practice.lead: Five gentle modules, ten playful activities. Go at your own pace, earn points and badges, and remember, every attempt is a win.
practice.card1_copy: Listen to the sound, then tap the shape it feels like. Round sounds are Bouba; sharp, spiky sounds are Kiki.
practice.card2_copy: Play each sound, then decide what kind of sound it was. You’re training your listening superpowers!
practice.question_short_long: Was that sound short or long?
practice.m2_copy: Gentle breathing and steady sounds that build voice control.
practice.m3_copy: Listen, move your body, and feel the rhythm of sound.
practice.m4_copy: Practice using your voice out loud, at your own pace.
practice.m5_copy: Put ideas in order and finish stories.
practice.listen_first: Tap the play button to listen first.
practice.done_copy: You finished this activity and earned 20 bonus points.

practice.mic_note: The microphone only listens for how loud your voice is. Nothing is recorded or saved.

practice.mic_denied_say: We couldn't use the microphone. Say the words out loud, then tap the button.
practice.mic_denied_record: We couldn't use the microphone. Please allow microphone access in your browser and try again.
practice.a3_copy: Take a big breath, then hum “mmmm” or say “ahhh”. Keep your sound going to fill the balloon!
practice.a4_copy: Follow the circle: breathe in as it grows, breathe out as it shrinks. Three calm breaths.
practice.a5_copy: Listen to the drum, then tap it the same number of times. You can clap or stomp along too!
practice.a6_copy: Reach up high for a high sound, touch your toes for a low sound, then tap your answer.
practice.a6_question: Was that sound high or low?
practice.a7_copy: Read the words out loud in your brave voice. The microphone listens for your voice.
practice.a8_copy: Record yourself saying anything you like: your name, a favorite word, or a song. Then listen back! Your recording stays on this device and is never uploaded.

practice.a9_copy: Tap the pictures in the order they happen: first, next, last.

science.title: Why sound, shape, and movement belong together
science.copy: Shape My Sound is built on a well-studied quirk of human perception, and on the science of how children learn best: through play and their whole bodies.
science.path_title: From a single sound to confident expression
science.step1_copy: A spoken sound: a soft “mmm” or a sharp “kee.”
science.step2_copy: The sound becomes a shape: round for Bouba, spiky for Kiki.
science.step3_copy: The child traces and moves with the shape, linking body to sound.
science.step4_copy: Sound, shape, and motion combine into confident speech.
science.bk_copy1: Show people a rounded blob and a spiky star, then ask which is “Bouba” and which is “Kiki.” Across cultures and languages, almost everyone agrees: the round one is Bouba, the spiky one is Kiki.
science.bk_copy2: That shared instinct reveals a deep link between what we hear and what we see. Shape My Sound uses it to give abstract sounds a friendly, visible form children can recognize, trace, and master.
science.principle1_copy: Engaging sound, sight, and movement together builds stronger, more durable memories than sound alone.
science.principle2_copy: Low-stakes play lowers anxiety, and a calm nervous system is far more ready to learn and take risks.
science.principle3_copy: Every interaction is shaped with speech-language professionals to stay safe, gentle, and effective.

founder.title: The Story Behind Shape My Sound
founder.portrait_alt: Kaabir Jaisingh, founder of Shape My Sound
founder.meet_copy1: Kaabir Jaisingh is a speaker, performer, athlete, and social impact founder focused on communication, confidence, and opportunity.
founder.meet_copy2: He is the founder of EmpowerHER, a TEDx featured, research based initiative supporting women artisans through confidence, communication, and greater visibility. He is also a National Elocution Excellence Awardee, Trinity Speech & Drama Performer, and ITF & National Tennis Scholar, with experience in public speaking, performance, and competitive tennis at national and international levels.
founder.meet_copy3: His work has also taken him to the TEDx stage, where he delivered The Art of Confidence: Voices in the Making (EmpowerHER), reflecting on his own experience with communication and the role confidence plays in finding and using your voice.
founder.tedx_alt: Kaabir Jaisingh speaking on stage at TEDxYouth@OIS
founder.began_copy1: Kaabir’s connection with communication began at the age of two and a half, when he experienced a speech delay. Speech therapy became an important part of his early development, helping him find greater clarity and confidence in expressing himself.
founder.began_copy2: Over time, communication became more than a skill. It became a way to perform, connect, and be heard. That journey led to one simple question:
founder.question: What if speech practice could feel more like play?
founder.idea_title: The Idea Behind Shape My Sound
founder.idea_copy1: That question became Shape My Sound, a multisensory experience where children explore speech through sound, shape, movement, and play.
founder.idea_copy2: Built around exploration and repetition, Shape My Sound aims to make speech practice more engaging, approachable, and enjoyable.
founder.idea_copy3: For Kaabir, it brings the journey full circle. Having once needed support to find his voice, he is now creating a space for children to explore theirs through an accessible, easy to use online platform.
founder.cta_title: Ready to help your child find their voice?
